tabs.tab1_description:
14 Mukhi Javanese Rudraksha is blessed with courage, confidence and success. It is called ‘Devmani’ meaning ‘The Gem of the Gods.’ It helps to overcome odds and attain success and victory. It blesses the wearer with stability in personal and professional life. This rudraksha is related with excellence in all aspects of life. This means outstanding performance and extraordinary talents rather than ordinary or average level of achievement and task accomplishment.

The Indonesian 14 mukhi rudraksha is claimed to have originated directly from Mahadev's eyes and is hence associated with both Lord Hanuman and Lord Shiva. This connection is easier to fathom given that Lord Hanuman is an incarnation of Lord Shiva. Hanuman was embodied and incarnated to eradicate evil forces. He fought on the side of Lord Rama. He aided Lord Rama in his war against the demon Ravana so that Sita Devi could be retrieved. Hanuman flew across the vast ocean to find her. No evil force could even approach Hanuman due to the intensity of his devotion. His victory was the result of a tremendous amount of devotion. He is the god of self-discipline, intelligence, courage, and strength.

The 14 mukhi Javanese Rudraksha is the most divine gem among the gems. Its wearer is blessed with ultimate Victory beyond any difficulty life throws at him.

According to ancient scriptures, the 14 mukhi Java Rudraksha greatly enhances the present, rectifies past karmas, and confers a positive, bright future. It is also endowed with superior decision-making abilities that guarantee success. This rudraksha assists the wearer in attaining the favor of Lord Shiva and Lord Hanuman. Lord Shiva is addressed as Mahadev which means the God of the Gods.

Scriptural Reference of 14 mukhi Rudraksha

Shiva Purana. Chapter 25, Sloka 80.

Chaturdashamukho yo hi Rudrakshah paramah shivah |
Dharayenmurghina tam bhaktya sarvapapam pranasyati || 80 ||
Fourteen faced Rudraksha is the form of great Shiva. It should respectfully be worn on the head which will cleanse all sins. 

Padma Purana, Chapter 59, summary from verses 143–146, 148:

चतुर्दशमुखो यो हि रुद्राक्षः परमः शिवः।
शिरसि धारयेद्यस्तु स याति परमं पदम्॥
देवाः सदा पूजयन्ति चतुर्दशमुखं सदा।
शिवस्य तुल्यः स भवति नात्र संशयः॥

Translation: The Rudraksha with fourteen faces is the Supreme Shiva. Whoever wears it on the head attains the highest state. The gods always worship the fourteen-faced Rudraksha. The wearer becomes like Shiva—there is no doubt about this.

Devi Bhagavata Purana, Skandha 11, Chapter 4, summary:

यः शिरसि चतुर्दशमुखं रुद्राक्षं धारयति, स शिवतुल्यो भवति।
देवाः तं पूजयन्ति, स शिवलोकं प्राप्नोति।

Translation: Whoever always wears the fourteen-faced Rudraksha on the head becomes like Shiva. The gods pay their respects to him, and he ultimately attains the highest goal, the state of Shiva.

14 mukhi Java Rudraksha is available in a variety of sizes, including: small, regular, large and collector. The bigger the size of the rudraksha the faster the results. This is because the seeds are bigger and the surface area in contact with skin is larger, thus, energy is dispersed more quickly throughout the body.

Nevertheless, the 14 mukhi Java Rudraksha is best worn as a 108+1 beads regular size mala on the chest, because this creates a powerful energy circuit in contact with a larger part of the body, and its energy is better dispersed through its sumeru bead resulting in a higher and faster healing potential and superior effectiveness than wearing a single 14 mukhi bead alone.

14 mukhi Rudraksha Price from Java, Indonesia

Although the price of any Rudraksha depends on its rarity, Rudra Centre offers authentic 14 mukhi Rudraksha from Java at an affordable price. Since it is an agricultural product the harvest of any season determines the price and this can vary from season to season. Rudra Centre sources all our Rudraksha directly from farmers in Java, our beads undergo a strict selection process where the size, health, weight and many other relevant parameters of the rudraksha are analysed, since we are the biggest suppliers of Java Rudraksha in the world, we are able to provide the best quality Rudraksha at the most reasonable fourteen mukhi rudraksha price to our customers.

As per our research bigger sized beads work faster. Bigger sized beads are rarer, so they are higher priced than smaller sized beads. As per the size of the bead, the Javanese 14 mukhi rudraksha is classified into small, regular, large & collector. These factors will determine the final 14 faced rudraksha price.

The original 14 mukhi Rudraksha price from Java ranges between INR 5000 – INR 14000 (USD 62.50 – USD 175) depending on their size. There may be some unique well-formed big sized 14 mukhi Javanese Rudraksha beads which come under the Super Collector variety which are priced as per their rarity.

There is another variety of 14 mukhi Java which are primarily used in Malas and Bracelets which are called 14 mukhi Malas or Bracelets. We offer a variety of these 14 mukhi java malas strung in silver caps or with sandalwood beads. These small Mukhi Malas are ideal for Japa - Keeping count of Mantra Chanting. The price of these malas ranges between USD 1.121 – USD 2.337 and the 14 mukhi rudraksha price in India for these malas from Rudra Centre ranges between INR 89,700 and INR 1,87,000.

Difference Between 14 mukhi Java & 14 mukhi Nepal

While the internal structure of both 14 mukhi from Java and Nepal is identical, the outer structure differs, 14 mukhi Nepal is bigger with deeper grooves or Mukhi lines and is more thorny with several projections whereas 14 mukhi Java are smaller, with thread like Mukhi lines which are not deep and have smoother surface.

Both beads emit same frequency and work on the same principles, in other words, both are 14 mukhi rudraksha original beads. The only difference is in the intensity of the frequency emitted because Nepali 14 mukhi is larger in size when compared to 14 mukhi Java. Therefore 14 mukhi Nepal works faster than 14 mukhi Java. Note that experience of the effects of Rudraksha is also a subjective experience however feedback from clients over 20 years have shown that Nepali beads work faster than Javanese beads. Long term effects of both beads are similar as the Chakra gets balanced due to resonance. The 14 mukhi Nepalese beads usually take 2-3 days to achieve resonance with the body whereas 14 mukhi Javanese beads take up to 10 – 12 days, during this time the thoughts process becomes clear and streamlined, however measurable results are experienced over months of usage.

Also, the price of Nepalese 14 mukhi is higher than Javanese 14 mukhi because the firstly the demand for Nepalese beads is higher than Javanese beads, also Javanese beads yields is much higher than Nepalese beads that means more Java beads are produced in an year than Nepalese beads hence the price of 14 mukhi Java Indonesia is lower than 14 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha.

While Nepalese beads are striking eye-catching in appearance due to its larger size, prominent thorns and shadowy deep grooves, making them generally more appealing for encasing in stunning silver or gold bracelets, Java beads are generally more suitable for intricated combinations with gemstones of smaller size and for threading malas and other accessories such as mats or meditation hats. Likewise, while Nepal beads are round shaped, Java beads are collected in a variety of geometric shapes.

Finally, it is an individual’s preference of whether he wants to wear 14 mukhi from Nepal or from Java Indonesia. Some like the power, intensity and deep grooves of Nepalese beads whereas some prefer Javanese beads as they can be converted into beautiful jewellery such as rings and earrings due to their smaller size, and are more comfortable to wear on the body due to their soft touch, and can be covered easily.

How to identify original 14 mukhi Java Indonesian Rudraksha?

Some fraudulent tests have gained popularity and must be avoided because their results are unreliable and they cannot be used to determine the authenticity of Rudraksha.

The Fake tests are the Water Test, Milk test or Copper Coin Rotation Test. All these tests are unscientific and produce untrustworthy results.

One way to determine the originality of Rudraksha beads is to take an X-ray. In an X-ray, the compartment and seeds inside the Rudraksha are observable, and their number should ideally correspond to the number of Mukhi lines on the bead. Sometimes all seeds are not visible as they get compressed during formation and compartments are very close to each other, though.

Experts at Rudra Centre can examine the bead and determine if they are original or not. You can send us images and videos of your Rudraksha at the email: contact@rudracentre.com for our experts to determine authenticity.

In recent years, numerous laboratories that offer rudraksha bead certification have emerged; however, these are highly unreliable because they lack the necessary expertise and frequently make errors when identifying rudraksha beads. Numerous dealers use these laboratories to issue counterfeit certificates. These laboratories are incapable of distinguishing manipulated beads in which additional lines are engraved on the original rudraksha bead to increase its mukhi and increase its price. Additionally, they do not disregard beads with incomplete mukhi lines that do not produce results. These laboratories are not affiliated with any central organization or government, so they lack credibility.

In order to protect customers, Rudra Centre has set up its own laboratory and started giving out authentic certificates that look at all aspects of Rudraksha. We check to see if the beads are in good shape, if the mukhi lines are all there, and if the rudraksha beads have been wrought in any way.

At Rudra Centre, we issue certificates for all beads procured from us. If you want an X-ray certificate for the Rudraksha bead, then an additional INR 500 (USD 6.25) is charged per Rudraksha bead.

How to Clean & Maintain 14 mukhi Rudraksha from Java, Indonesia?

Rudraksha beads can last a lifetime and be passed down through generations if cared for properly.

In cold and dry climates, rudraksha beads may develop surface-level cracks, in which case any natural unscented oil may be applied, such as olive oil, sandal oil, or cow ghee.

Rudraksha may develop molds and insects if they are kept in a humid place and unused for a long time, in this case follow the below steps:

  • Dip the Rudraksha beads in lukewarm water for 15 mins.
  • Clean any molds visible of the surface using a toothbrush.
  • Dry them under the shade of the Sun (indirect Sunlight) or you can also use a dryer or hairdryer.
  • After following the above steps, you can start wearing your rudraksha beads or combination again.

Follow the steps below to regularly clean your Rudraksha beads:

  • Wash Rudraksha beads under running water.
  • Scrub the surface of the rudraksha to remove any dust particles caught in the grooves, using a toothbrush.
  • Use the shade of the Sun (indirect sunlight) or a hairdryer to dry the beads.
  • Apply any natural and unscented oil like Olive oil, Almond oil or Sandal oil.
  • If you are planning to not wear beads for a long duration, it is advisable to keep them in the fridge.
  • Do not use any chemical cleaner or insecticide or pesticide to clean or treat your Rudraksha.
  • Do not put your rudraksha beads in boiling water or extremely hot water.

14 mukhi Java, Indonesian Rudraksha Health & Color

The 14 mukhi Java rudraksha color ranges from white to dark brown hue. This is a natural process that has no impact on the energy of the Rudraksha bead. It is ideal to choose a light sandy brown to brown Rudraksha bead, as this indicates that the bead is healthy and newly harvested. It is recommended to avoid wearing dark black or dark grey beads, as they may lack vitality. If you hear the seeds within the bead rattling, the bead is lifeless or dead; if you do not hear any rattling, the bead is healthy and alive.

You can examine the bead from all sides and look inside the natural hole to ensure no white mold or insects have infested it. Soap sometimes gets stuck around the white lines or mukhis, or inside the natural holes of the bead. To prevent these chemicals to further damage the bead, clean the bead from these as soon as possible. The energy of the Rudraksha beads resides in the seeds, so we must ensure that they are alive and healthy.
